entities.summary: Autonomy refers to the concept found in moral, political, and bioethical philosophy, first articulated in ancient Greece and later developed by prominent thinkers such as John Locke, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, and Immanuel Kant. The idea of autonomy emphasizes the individual's inherent right to self-governance, freedom, and decision-making, shaping modern political and social systems. This concept has had a profound impact on the development of human rights, democracy, and the rule of law, influencing contemporary debates on bioethics, feminism, and social justice. Autonomy has also been linked to the growth of scientific inquiry and the emergence of new technologies, as individuals and communities assert their right to autonomy in the face of scientific and technological advancements. The concept of autonomy continues to evolve, informing contemporary discussions on artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and the future of work.
